statuses.playable: A person played it and confirmed gameplay.
statuses.title: Reached its title, login or main menu on screen; gameplay is not confirmed.
statuses.runs: Starts and runs a bounded session to its window and surface without a fatal error; no screen or gameplay confirmation is recorded.
statuses.blocked: Starts, then the app itself ends the session; the cause is outside the emulator's framework services.

com.kiloo.subwaysurf.name: Subway Surfers
com.kiloo.subwaysurf.evidence: The maintainer reports it is playable and its ads work (APKPure 3.70.3 build). On 2026-11-08 they ran it on a Steam Deck (SteamOS, Desktop mode; the Bifrost build was not recorded): 20 to 40 FPS, mostly 30 to 40, with stutters and a hot CPU but very stable, and close to 30 W of total system power during play (maintainer-reported). Two photos of the Deck's performance overlay are the only capture.
notes: Quitting through the game's own quit confirmation left the app running in the background on the Deck: its audio kept playing and Return to app did not show a window. Not traced and not reproduced here. After its last Activity finishes the launcher exits only once the app has no service of its own left, so a service that stays alive would explain it (unconfirmed). A photo of the overlay in that state reads about 1 FPS with a worst frame of 23 s, two CPU threads pinned (100% and 91%) at 90 C, the GPU idle and the battery at 14%.

In Game Mode on the Deck the maintainer got a black screen (not investigated). The library cannot simply be added as a non-Steam game: Steam's environment variables have to be unset first, or it cannot reach the Android library (maintainer-reported: LD_PRELOAD and related variables; the exact set was not recorded).

org.mozilla.firefox.name: Firefox
org.mozilla.firefox.evidence: Sessions reach the main Activity, a GPU window, first-run onboarding and a GeckoView surface, with tab, GPU and crash-helper child processes. The maintainer reports pages do not load.
notes: Most sessions end when a native Gecko thread reaches an in-process Java Binder service without a JVM attachment (JavaBinder: env null); which service is not identified. A general fix for that abort landed on 2026-11-01; Firefox has not been re-tested with it.
The first codec query blocks Gecko's main thread for 5 s waiting for media.player, which is not published, delaying the tab process by about 9 s.
Firefox sends its own telemetry and, when accepted in its dialog, crash reports to Mozilla.

com.google.android.youtube.name: YouTube
com.google.android.youtube.evidence: The maintainer's screenshot shows the home screen (logo, search bar and the Home, Shorts, Subscriptions and You tabs). Later sessions that day searched and played video while its frame conversion was profiled. The maintainer has not reported it as playable.
notes: Shorts in a landscape window and the signed-in feed are not confirmed.

Its onStop ended the app until isPackageSuspendedForUser was answered, and the first video codec on each new video view lost its queue and was restarted until the SurfaceView reader took any producer (both fixed 2026-11-08, from a session log of 2026-11-07; not yet run in YouTube).

com.HoYoverse.Nap.name: Zenless Zone Zero
com.HoYoverse.Nap.evidence: The maintainer played it past login, shader compilation and the loading screen into the city and says it works, with very low-resolution textures and heavy lag. Sampled frames of their screen recording show Sixth Street, dialogue and the map, and one session ran 44 minutes with no crash. It needed the guest-memory fix in the changelog: before it, its WebView aborted within about a minute of every stock run. On 2026-11-08 the maintainer played its story scenes with the ASTC-to-BC7 path; two overlay screenshots read 29 and 30 FPS at 3440x1384, 6.1 GB session RAM and 4.2 to 4.3 of 8.6 GB VRAM, and the maintainer said the image looked the same as before and the models were always very low resolution.
notes: The frame rate is low: the overlay read roughly 4 to 30 FPS in the gameplay frames I read, and 0 to 2 FPS on the long loading screen after Press to Play. A 3-minute BIFROST_PROF run (the last 90 s in gameplay) spent 58 to 81% of CPU time in translated code with at most 2.7 of 12 host threads busy. Whether the JIT or something else sets the frame rate is not established.

Textures are very low resolution (maintainer-reported, before and after the ASTC change); the cause is not established. Until 2026-11-08 the host GPU's missing ASTC support made Unity log that it was decompressing ASTC_6x6 textures; the thunk now offers ASTC through BC7 and that message no longer appears, with no visible change in image quality. The 3D scene is soft while the UI text is crisp, which fits a low render scale or quality tier, and the emulated device reports an unknown model (device model "unknown", the ranchu SoC and 8 GiB), which a game may grade as low-end. The game's saved graphics settings are not readable from outside it; the render-target size has not been traced.

The ASTC transcoder used 60 to 70% of the game's CPU samples in two passive profiles of story scenes on 2026-11-08 (before its helper threads were given the lowest priority and a cache of finished transcodes was added; the cache's hit rate in a game is not measured).
Maximizing the window leaves the progress bar frozen until the window is restored, while the rest of the screen keeps animating (maintainer-reported, not investigated).

A null dereference in libunity (libunity+0x72d350) ended two heavily traced startup sessions; it was not seen in stock sessions. On 2026-11-08 a stock session ended on another guest null dereference (pc 0x7153f5c0, about 2.5 minutes after launch, with no ASTC or Vulkan fault in its log); a relaunch with the crash dump on ran more than 7 minutes without it, and an earlier session the same day on the build without the ASTC path ended on one at pc 0x71dbf774. The module was not named: the crash line now names it from the guest's mappings.

com.serenityforge.dokidokiliteratureclub.name: Doki Doki Literature Club
com.serenityforge.dokidokiliteratureclub.evidence: The maintainer played it into the story (dialogue and a Yes/No choice, in screenshots) on 2026-11-06. Ren'Py 8.4.1 reached its interface in about 12 s and sessions ran up to 3 minutes with exit status 0.
notes: The audio popped in the runs the maintainer checked on 2026-11-06. It is not AAudio's sample format (the game asks for FLOAT and gets FLOAT). The pushed PCM had a discontinuity every 1024 frames: SDL's AAudio backend writes with a 1 ms timeout and discards a short write, and the thunk returned short counts on a full ring. Android's legacy path blocks until everything is written. The write path now does too; after the fix the same segment of captured PCM shows no boundary clicks (about 1.3x the background curvature, from about 190x). The maintainer listened to the fixed build on 2026-11-08 and confirmed the audio is clean.

Resizing the window corrupts the graphics: afterwards backgrounds, sprites and the textbox draw black while text still draws (maintainer screenshots). Traced on 2026-11-08: Ren'Py's on_resize deletes every GL texture on Android (TextureLoader.init calls quit) and keeps drawing the old names, because it re-uploads them only when pygame_sdl2 reports a recreated GL context, and SDL leaves the context alone on a size-only surfaceChanged. This is the game's own resize path, not a mistranslated GL call; whether a real device behaves the same was not checked. The app therefore carries a built-in default of Window: "Keep the app's shape" (window_mode keep, which a saved choice overrides): the maintainer confirmed the images stay with it at 2026-11-08.
